a novel fluoroquinoline 7l was identified as a promising candidate for the development of new drugs for tuberculosis treatment.
the 7-(sub secondary piperidyl)-1-clopropyl-1,4- dihydro-6-fluorquinolones are the most promising antimycobacterial agents.

the design, synthesis and evaluation of novel fluoroquionolones as potent antimycobacterial agents against MDR-TB.
the development of novel fluoroquionolones for the treatment of tuberculosis.
the design and synthesis of new fluoroquinolone derivatives with improved antimycobacterial activities.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the novel fluoroquinoline compounds are promising antimycobacterial agents.
7l has the most potent antimycobacterial activity among the tested compounds.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the novel 7-(subsecondary amino)quinolones with cyclopropyl and t-butyl groups on phenyl ring at C1 position are potent antimycobacterial compounds and 7l is a promising candidate for the development of a new generation fluoroquinolone for the treatment of MDR-TB.
the introduction of the piperidyl moiety into the quinolone nucleus resulted in compounds with improved antimycobacterial activity.
the synthesized compounds are potent antimycobacterial agents, especially compound 7l which has a potential for further development as a new drug candidate against MDR-TB.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the introduction of a cyclopropyl group at C1-position in the 1,4-dialkyl-7-(substituted piperazin-1- yl)-6-fluoroquinolone series has led to compounds with potent antimycobacterial activities.
7l can be a potential lead for the development of new antimycobacterial agents with improved activity and safety profiles.
the novel 7l is the most active fluoroquinolone in this series against M. tuberculosis H37Rb and MDR-Tb.
